notes.heading: Overview of Cellular Respiration
notes.body: Cells break down glucose to make ATP. Overall equation: C6H12O6 + 6 O2 -> 6 CO2 + 6 H2O + energy. Eukaryotes get roughly 30-32 ATP per glucose.

notes.heading: Krebs Cycle
notes.body: In the mitochondrial matrix. Acetyl-CoA joins oxaloacetate to make citrate. Per glucose (two turns of the cycle): 2 ATP, 6 NADH, 2 FADH2 and 4 CO2.
notes.quote: 3. Krebs cycle (citric acid cycle) - In the mitochondrial matrix. Acetyl-CoA joins oxaloacetate to make citrate. - Per glucose (two turns of the cycle): 2 ATP, 6 NADH, 2 FADH2 and 4 CO2

notes.heading: Exam Traps
notes.body: Most ATP comes from the electron transport chain, not from glycolysis or the Krebs cycle. CO2 is released in pyruvate oxidation and in the Krebs cycle: 6 CO2 per glucose in total. The water in the overall equation is made at the end of the electron transport chain, not in glycolysis.
